Order the clusters of an alluvial to reduce crossing flows

Source: R/minimize_crossing_alluvial.R
minimize_crossing_alluvial.Rd

In an alluvial plot, flows between clusters drawn far apart cross many other flows and make the plot unreadable. minimize_crossing_alluvial() computes an order of the clusters that places clusters exchanging many nodes next to each other. It is a heuristic, not an optimal solution to the crossing problem.

The order is built in two steps. First, the function builds a network of clusters: two clusters are tied when nodes move from one to the other between windows, with a cosine weight \(n_{ab} / \sqrt{\bar{s}_a \bar{s}_b}\), \(n_{ab}\) being the number of moving nodes and \(\bar{s}_a\) the mean size of cluster \(a\) over its windows. It removes the ties one by one, from the weakest to the strongest, and records at each step the connected component of each cluster. Clusters are ordered by this sequence of components: clusters that stay together until the strongest ties are removed end up side by side. This groups clusters that exchange nodes, but it does not count the crossings.

Second (refine = TRUE, the default), the order is improved against the crossings themselves. For each pair of consecutive windows, the flows are the numbers of nodes going from a cluster of the first window to a cluster of the second; two flows cross when the order of their origins and the order of their destinations are opposite, and the pair is weighted by the product of the two flows. Each cluster in turn is moved to the position that minimises the total, until no move helps. This is a local search, which can end in a local optimum, and which costs more with many clusters and flows.

Usage

minimize_crossing_alluvial(
  alluv_dt,
  intertemporal_cluster_column = NULL,
  node_id = NULL,
  window_column = "window",
  refine = TRUE,
  max_passes = 10,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

alluv_dt

A data frame created with networks_to_alluv(), whose rows follow the chronological order of the windows (the order of the levels of window_column if it is a factor, as in networks_to_alluv(), or of their appearance).

intertemporal_cluster_column

Character scalar, the column with the dynamic clusters.

node_id

Character scalar, the column with the node identifiers.

window_column

Character scalar, the column with the time windows ("window" by default).

refine

Logical. If TRUE (default), refines the order against the crossings (see the description); if FALSE, keeps the order of the components.

max_passes

Whole number, the maximum number of passes of the refinement over all the clusters.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE (default), reports the weighted number of crossings before and after the refinement.

Value

alluv_dt with a new column minimize_crossing_order, the rank of each cluster, that plot_alluvial() uses to order the blocks.

Details

The alluvial method (following clusters over time with networks_to_alluv(), minimize_crossing_alluvial() and plot_alluvial()) was initiated by Alexandre Truc.

Examples

networks <- build_dynamic_networks(
  nodes = subset(Nodes_stagflation, source_type == "Stagflation"),
  directed_edges = Ref_stagflation,
  source_id = "source_id",
  target_id = "target_id",
  time_variable = "source_year",
  time_window = 10,
  method = "similarity",
  edges_threshold = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
#> Warning: The last window is shorter than the others.
#> ℹ The data end in "2013", but the last window ends in "2014".
networks <- add_clusters(
  networks,
  clustering_method = "leiden",
  objective_function = "modularity",
  seed = 123,
  verbose = FALSE
)
networks <- merge_dynamic_clusters(
  networks,
  cluster_id = "cluster_leiden",
  node_id = "source_id",
  method = "majority", threshold_similarity = 0.51,
  similarity_type = "partial"
)
#> ℹ Linking clusters across windows with the "majority" rule: a cluster inherits
#>   the identifier of a past cluster when more than 0.51 of the nodes of each go
#>   to / come from the other (double majority). The comparison counts the nodes
#>   present in both windows only (`similarity_type` = "partial").
#> Warning: 3 pairs of consecutive windows share no node: their clusters cannot be matched.
#> ℹ Clusters are matched through the nodes they share. In a network of documents
#>   (coupling), each node has one date: the windows must overlap (`window_step`
#>   smaller than `time_window` in `build_dynamic_networks()`). If windows already
#>   overlap, the nodes may have changed completely, or the threshold may leave a
#>   window without edges.
alluv_dt <- networks_to_alluv(
  networks,
  intertemporal_cluster_column = "dynamic_cluster_leiden",
  node_id = "source_id"
)
#> ℹ No color column in the graphs: no colour kept (see `color_alluvial()`).
#> ℹ No cluster_label column in the graphs: no label kept (see `name_clusters()`).

alluv_dt <- minimize_crossing_alluvial(
  alluv_dt,
  intertemporal_cluster_column = "dynamic_cluster_leiden",
  node_id = "source_id"
)
#> Warning: no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
#> ℹ Weighted crossings of the flows between windows: 0 with the order of the
#>   links, 0 after the refinement.
unique(alluv_dt[, c("dynamic_cluster_leiden", "minimize_crossing_order")])
#> Key: <dynamic_cluster_leiden>
#>     dynamic_cluster_leiden minimize_crossing_order
#>                     <char>                   <int>
#>  1:                   cl_1                       1
#>  2:                  cl_10                       9
#>  3:                  cl_11                      10
#>  4:                  cl_12                      12
#>  5:                  cl_13                      13
#>  6:                  cl_14                      14
#>  7:                  cl_15                      15
#>  8:                   cl_2                       2
#>  9:                   cl_3                       3
#> 10:                   cl_4                       4
#> 11:                   cl_5                       5
#> 12:                   cl_6                       6
#> 13:                   cl_7                       7
#> 14:                   cl_8                       8
#> 15:                   cl_9                      11
